status: tested in the law pilot (21 Nov 2026, 3 papers)
setting: An invented country with its own courts and statutes. No real legal system is assumed: courts have a level, decisions relate to sources by three generic relations. All names are invented.

court.about: a court of the invented country

provision.about: a statutory provision, e.g. 'section 9 of the <Name> Act <year>'; alt names like 'section 9', 's. 9'

relies_on.meaning: the decision uses the source as a basis for its ruling

distinguishes.meaning: the decision says an earlier decision does not apply because the facts differ

rejects.meaning: the decision refuses to accept the source as a basis for its ruling

questions.text: Which sources did the court rely on in {s}?
Which decisions treated {o} as a valid basis, and which did not?

world_notes: Make 3 courts at different levels, 4-8 provisions of 1-2 invented statutes on one area of law, and enough decisions (years 2010-2025) that each paper has its own mix. A decision may only rely on, distinguish or reject EARLIER decisions. Plant disagreements: two decisions that treat the same provision in opposite ways (one relies on it, one rejects it).
